title: Block: A Linked List Walk With a Dummy Node
oneLiner: Remove every node holding a given value from a linked list, using a dummy node so the head is not a special case.
keyTakeaway: A dummy node in front of the head means every real node has a predecessor, so deleting the head looks like deleting anything else. Return dummy.next, not head.
explanation:
Return the head of the list with every node whose value equals val removed. The head itself, or every node, may need to go.

Create a dummy node pointing at head and walk a pointer from the dummy. While pointer.next exists: if it holds val, link past it (pointer.next = pointer.next.next) and stay where you are, because the new next might also match; otherwise step forward. The answer is dummy.next.

starterCode.python:
# ListNode: val, next, ListNode(val, next=None) (provided)
def remove_value(head, val):
    # 1. Make a dummy node whose next is the head, so removing the head is not a special case.
    # 2. Start a pointer at the dummy.
    # 3. While the pointer has a next node: if that node holds the value, link past it and stay put.
    # 4. Otherwise move the pointer forward one node.
    # 5. Return the dummy's next, the new head.
    return head

gotchas: Moving the pointer forward after unlinking, which skips the next node when two matches are adjacent.
Returning head instead of dummy.next when the old head was removed.

complexity.note: One walk down the list; the dummy and one pointer are the only extra nodes.
